thread:
alice: FYI customer reported intermittent 502 + huge tail latency on /v1/embeddings when they enable dynamic batching and max_batch_size=256. Happens ~1-2x / 10k requests, not constant.

bob: Any reproducible steps or sample payloads?

alice: They sent ~200 short docs (avg 24 tokens) in parallel from our python SDK v0.9.1. Sample call: `client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-compact-3", input=[...])`. We saw backend logs: `Batcher: assembled batch 256 -> enqueue delay 120ms -> dispatch -> NACK: timeout_to_dispatch`.

samir: Can you paste the exact error from the API response? 502 vs 429 vs 500 matter.

alice: Response snippet: `{"error":{"message":"internal: route failure","code":502}}`. Also one instance showed `auth: token expired` for a different request at ~same minute, but customer confirmed token was valid.

yang: Two threads: (1) tail latency when large batches form and one shard is slow; (2) transient auth check failures due to JWT key rotation race. Might be correlated but separate root causes.

liz: Quick mitigation suggestions: set `max_batch_size=64` and `batch_timeout_ms=25` for that client, or pin them to a dedicated shard/pool. Can we try a config change first?

alice: Customer agreed to try `max_batch_size=64`. Also asked for repro steps so they can run locally. They want to know if this is a bug or expected behavior.

bob: For repro, ask them to: 1) send 10k parallel requests using same SDK/service account, 2) collect `X-Request-Id` for failed calls, 3) capture server-side `batch_id` from our traces (we can link). Share a minimal script.

samir: I dug through runtime traces for the minute in question. One GPU worker reported a KV cache eviction and GC spike: `GPU-0: model mem pressure -> slab reclaim -> stall 340ms` while other GPUs completed their slices. When one worker stalls, coalesced batch waits up to `batch_timeout_ms` before splitting -> results in 500/502 on the client. This aligns with the `enqueue delay 120ms` log.

yang: That GC/eviction pattern could be triggered by large batch assembly + mixed-sequence lengths causing unexpected workspace allocation. We should check kernel selection and async copy contention for that model variant.

liz: For the auth blip: ops->auth recently rotated a key at 2026-04-21T12:03:00Z and our cache TTL is 30s; there could be a small window where cached verifiers reject new tokens. Ops already lowered TTL to 5s in staging. Recommend aligning with prod.

alice: Customer also mentioned billing spikes (unexpected token usage) tied to retries. They saw duplicate downstream requests during 502s. Any short-term billing advice?

bob: We can issue an invoice credit for the affected window if they provide request ids. Also recommend client-side idempotency/ retry backoff to prevent duplicate bursts.

samir: Action items I can take: 1) correlate `batch_id`s for the failed request ids and produce per-shard latency histograms; 2) capture worker-level GPU mem/GC logs for that 10 minute window; 3) add a runtime guard to preemptively split overly-large coalesced batches if a single worker's enqueue time > threshold.

yang: I'll reproduce locally with a stress script that mirrors their token length distribution + parallelism. If I can reproduce, we can test kernel scheduling patches.

liz: Ops: please confirm auth key rotation TTL change in prod and whether any clients saw verification errors.

ci-bot: build/infra-deploy succeeded for `runtime/2026-04-20` (commit `a1b2c3`)

deploy-bot: deploy to prod started at 2026-04-21T12:10:00Z; rolling 5/20 workers in shard-3

alice: Temp mitigation communicated to customer: lower max_batch_size to 64 and reduce batch_timeout_ms; we'll follow up once we have shard traces. They applied change and reported no further 502s in the next hour.

bob: Keep this thread updated. If we confirm a runtime scheduling bug, label as P1 and open a postmortem with owner `eng-runtime`.

samir: Uploaded initial latency histograms and GPU logs to the trace link: https://internal/trace/xyz (shared). Preliminary: shard-3 had 99.9p enqueue=380ms for coalesced batches >200.

alice: Thanks everyone — forwarding notes to the customer success rep for credits + follow-up.

liz: Next steps: (1) Ops confirm auth TTL change in prod; (2) Samir & Yang attempt repro and propose guard; (3) Bob coordinate billing credit once request ids are listed.

alice: Closing for now since immediate mitigation worked; will reopen if new failures surface. :white_check_mark:
